__faion_header__.purpose: The EARS grammar as data: patterns, clause ranks, cardinality, head-marker regexes and the full E/W/I rule table with a dated citation per rule.
__faion_header__.consumes: nothing at runtime; authored from the EARS notation dossier (2026-08-03) and its primary sources
__faion_header__.produces: the single source of truth loaded by scripts/validate-ears-requirements.py and embedded by the Go runtime (faion-cli internal/earslint) via go:embed
__faion_header__.depends-on: content/01-core-rules.xml (r1, r2, r3, r4), templates/ears-fixtures.tsv (both implementations must reproduce it byte-for-byte)
__faion_header__.token-budget-impact: medium — load only when writing or auditing the linter, not when writing requirements

notation_version: unversioned; five patterns unchanged since Mavin et al., IEEE RE'09 (2009)
regex_dialect: RE2-safe: no backreferences, no lookaround. Python's re accepts every expression here; Go's regexp accepts them unchanged.

patterns.semantics: A fundamental property of the system. No precondition, no trigger, always active.
Active while the system is in a specific state. A state persists; it has duration.
patterns.source: Mavin, fetched 2026-08-03; 'or optionally the keyword During' per Terzakis, Intel, ICCGI 2013

patterns.semantics: Initiated when and only when a trigger occurs or is detected. An event is instantaneous and expected.

patterns.template: Where <feature is included>, the <system name> shall <system response>
patterns.semantics: Invoked only in systems that include the optional feature. Build or plan configuration, NOT runtime state.

patterns.template: If <trigger>, then the <system name> shall <system response>
patterns.semantics: Handles unwanted behaviour: error conditions, failures, faults, disturbances, undesired events.
patterns.source: Mavin, fetched 2026-08-03; the only pattern with a second obligatory keyword

patterns.template: <multiple condition clauses>, the <system name> shall <system response>
patterns.semantics: Two or more condition clauses combined. Legal, and bounded by the clause-order rule.
patterns.verification_hint: derive from the strongest clause present
patterns.source: Mavin complex form 'While <precondition(s)>, When <trigger>, ...'; Terzakis complex examples, both fetched 2026-08-03

clause_order.rule: Rank sequence across a statement's condition clauses must be non-decreasing; a condition keyword after the actor is a violation.
clause_order.derivation: DERIVED, not quoted. No primary source prints a total ordering of all four keywords. This is the unique order consistent with Mavin's 'While ... when ...' complex form plus Terzakis's 'Where ... when ...' (optical drive) and 'When ... if ... then ...' (landing gear) examples, all fetched 2026-08-03. If a primary source contradicts the Where<While edge, only that comparison moves and only E005 changes.

cardinality.if: 0..1, and requires a matching 'then' immediately before the actor
cardinality.source: Mavin generic ruleset: 'Zero or many preconditions; Zero or one trigger; One system name; One or many system responses', fetched 2026-08-03

pipeline.note: Not one monolithic regex per pattern. Monolithic patterns break on any condition clause containing a comma or the word 'the', and give useless error messages. The same three-stage decomposition is used by labeth/ears-lint-go (MIT, fetched 2026-08-03), arrived at independently.

regex.head_strict: (?i)(?:^|,\s*)(then\s+)?the\s+([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9 _/.-]{1,58}?)\s+(shall|must|will|should|may|can|might|has to|have to|needs to|need to|is able to)\s+
regex.head_lenient: (?i)(?:^|[,\s]\s*)(then\s+)?the\s+([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9 _/.-]{1,58}?)\s+(shall|must|will|should|may|can|might|has to|have to|needs to|need to|is able to)\s+
regex.weak_modal: (?i)^(must|will|should|may|can|might|has to|have to|needs to|need to|is able to)$
regex.escape_clause: (?i)\b(if possible|as appropriate|as required|as needed|where feasible|to the extent (?:practical|possible)|and so on|etc\.?)\b

note_on_bare_integer: The negative lookbehind/lookahead in bare_integer and number_with_unit is Python-only convenience; the Go implementation achieves the same exclusion by rejecting a digit run whose neighbouring byte is a word character, '/' or '-'. This keeps identifiers such as UTF-8, PDF/A-2b, HTTP/2 and ordinals such as 95th out of the numeric checks.

rules.test: no 'shall' token anywhere on the line
rules.message: no obligation stated: a requirement without 'shall' is a description
rules.citation: Mavin generic ruleset, fetched 2026-08-03

rules.test: more than one 'shall' token
rules.message: two 'shall' means two requirements; split into two identifiers
rules.citation: Mavin et al. RE'09 problem taxonomy: complexity, duplication
rules.short_circuit_reason: further linting of a bundled statement is noise; split first, then classify each half

rules.test: no 'the <system name> <modal>' head marker found
rules.message: no system actor: nobody is responsible for this behaviour
rules.citation: Terzakis, Intel, ICCGI 2013 — missing-actor class

rules.test: a condition clause does not open with while/during/when/where/if
rules.message: unparseable condition clause: it must open with an EARS keyword
rules.citation: Mavin, fetched 2026-08-03

rules.test: clause rank sequence decreases, OR a condition keyword appears in the response after the actor
rules.message: clause order violates Where < While < When < If/Then
rules.citation: Mavin: 'The clauses of a requirement written in EARS always appear in the same order', fetched 2026-08-03

rules.test: 'if' without matching 'then', or 'then' without 'if'
rules.message: the unwanted-behaviour pattern requires both 'If' and 'then'
rules.citation: Mavin unwanted-behaviour template, fetched 2026-08-03

rules.test: more than one where / when / if clause
rules.message: cardinality violated: at most one where, one when, one if
rules.citation: Mavin: 'Zero or one trigger', fetched 2026-08-03

rules.test: the head-marker modal is a weak modal rather than 'shall'
rules.message: weak modal instead of 'shall'; auto-fixable
rules.citation: RFC 2119 semantics; must/will/should/may are not obligations

rules.test: a condition contains both 'and' and 'or' with no parentheses
rules.message: mixed and/or without parentheses has no defined precedence
rules.citation: labeth/ears-lint-go boolean clause parser, fetched 2026-08-03

rules.test: the statement does not end with a period
rules.message: missing sentence terminator; cheap catch for truncation
rules.citation: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 sentence discipline

rules.test: response opens with be/been/being + past participle
rules.message: passive response hides who acts
rules.citation: Mavin et al. RE'09 problem taxonomy: ambiguity

rules.test: response contains ' and ' / ' or ' / 'and/or'
rules.message: compound response usually hides two requirements; split it
rules.citation: Mavin et al. RE'09 problem taxonomy: duplication

rules.test: a vague token is present
rules.message: vague language cannot be tested
rules.citation: Mavin et al. RE'09 problem taxonomy: vagueness. Strict superset of the five-token list previously inline in sdd/spec-requirements r5-no-vague-language

rules.test: an escape clause is present
rules.message: optional escape clause makes the requirement unverifiable
rules.citation: INCOSE Guide for Writing Requirements — optional escape clause rule

rules.test: response contains it/they/them/these/those
rules.message: ambiguous referent
rules.citation: Mavin et al. RE'09 problem taxonomy: ambiguity. Deliberately excludes 'this'/'that' — too many relative-clause false positives

rules.test: the 'if' body describes a normal user action
rules.message: 'If' used for an expected event; probably 'When'
rules.citation: heuristic, unmeasured — must remain a warning forever (see r5-if-vs-when-generated-not-guessed)

rules.test: the 'when' body describes a failure
rules.message: 'When' used for an unwanted condition; probably 'If ... then'
rules.citation: heuristic, unmeasured — must remain a warning forever

rules.test: an unquantified rate or latency word is present
rules.message: unquantified rate: needs a number and a unit
rules.citation: Mavin et al. RE'09 problem taxonomy: untestability

rules.test: response exceeds 30 words
rules.message: wordiness
rules.citation: Mavin et al. RE'09 problem taxonomy: wordiness

rules.test: more than three condition clauses
rules.message: excessive preconditions produce an unwieldy sentence; lift them into a state machine and write one requirement per transition
rules.citation: Wikipedia, Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax, limitations section, fetched 2026-08-03

rules.test: the system name is system/software/application/app/product/platform/tool/it/we
rules.message: unnamed component: legal EARS, useless traceability
rules.citation: practitioner rule — a requirement with no named component cannot be mapped to a test file or an owner

rules.test: response opens with support/handle/process/manage/deal with/take care of/address
rules.message: weasel verb: state what the system actually does
rules.citation: Terzakis, Intel, ICCGI 2013 — 'The software shall support a water level sensor. What does the word support mean?'

rules.test: response contains a bare integer and no integer paired with a unit
rules.message: number without a unit
rules.citation: Mavin et al. RE'09 problem taxonomy: untestability

rules.test: the statement classified as ubiquitous and emitted no error
rules.message: most requirements are not ubiquitous — is there an unstated trigger or precondition here?
rules.citation: Terzakis, Intel, ICCGI 2013: 'Question ubiquitous requirements ... Most requirements are not ubiquitous'

modes.default: warnings-only, exit 0. Errors are reported; the process still succeeds.
modes.strict: opt-in, CI-only. Any E-code fails the run; E010 is promoted to error. Do not enable before the rule set has been run over a real corpus and tuned.
modes.lenient: accepts a bare space before the actor, so Kiro-style comma-less ALL-CAPS 'WHEN ... THE SYSTEM SHALL ...' parses. Accepted, never canonicalised.
modes.fix: handles exactly one class safely — E008 modal normalisation to 'shall'. Nothing else is auto-fixable without changing meaning.

not_covered: correctness — a statement can parse clean and be a catastrophic bug
completeness of the set — an 'If X' with no 'not X' counterpart needs a separate set-level coverage pass
consistency — two requirements can each be valid EARS and contradict each other
temporal richness — EARS has no 'until', no 'for the duration of', no 'at most N times per'; all of it smuggles into free-text response where no rule can see it
localisation — the keyword table is English; questions localise, stored syntax does not

prior_art.detail: automated EARS templating and compliance checking since v2.10, announced 2019-08-21; NLP-based; DOORS Next / Jama / Polarion / Word / Excel
MIT Go library: shell parsing, pattern classification, boolean clause parser, catalog matching, clause-order and vague-language rules. 0 stars
MIT Vale style package: ears.Syntax, ears.Shall, ears.PassiveVoice, ears.WeakWords. Requires Vale as an external binary
EARS is a writing convention in requirements.md; no validate/lint/parse language anywhere in the docs
issue #1356 'Feature Request: EARS Integration', opened 2025-12-20, closed without implementation

positioning: The defensible claim is 'the first EARS validator that runs inside your coding agent — one binary, no DOORS, no Jama, no seat licence.' Never 'nobody has built this': QVscribe has machine-validated EARS since 2019 and labeth/ears-lint-go exists.
unaudited_surfaces: As of 2026-08-04 the VS Code Marketplace, StrictDoc, Doorstop and rmtoo have NOT been checked for EARS grammar support (the 2026-08-03 research pass exhausted its search budget, and a re-check on 2026-08-04 could not run for the same reason). Any of them could weaken the segment claim. Re-verify before this positioning appears in customer-facing copy.
